RITES Limited.desc: Indian engineering and transport consultancy, working on railways, roads, metros, airports and ports from design to commissioning, and acting as the export arm of Indian Railways for locomotives and coaches. It is a listed state-owned company under India's Ministry of Railways, incorporated in 1974, and says it has worked on more than 5,000 projects for clients in over 55 countries.

sources.title: About Us

Ircon International Limited.desc: Indian construction company that builds railways, highways and bridges on a turnkey basis. It was set up by the Ministry of Railways in 1976 as Indian Railway Construction Company Limited, later renamed, and its shares were listed on the NSE and BSE in September 2018; its own site says turnover passed Rs 10,000 crore in 2023.

sources.title: Ircon International Limited (home and achievements)

Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mocambique.desc: Mozambique's state ports and railways company, created out of a state enterprise by Decree 40/94 of 1994 and holding public-law status. Its 2010 corporate profile says it directly runs the southern railway lines to Ressano Garcia, Goba and Limpopo (about 700 km in total), the port of Pemba and the fuel terminals at Maputo, Beira and Nacala, with the central and northern lines and other ports handed to concessionaires.

sources.title: CFM Corporate Profile
sources.publisher: Portos e Caminhos de Ferro de Mocambique, E.P. (CFM)

Organisation pour la Mise en Valeur du f.desc: Intergovernmental body that manages the Senegal River basin, set up by a convention signed at Nouakchott on 11 March 1972 by Mali, Mauritania and Senegal, with Guinea joining later. Member states jointly own the dams and other works it runs; a World Bank account says these produce about 800 GWh of electricity a year, could irrigate 375,000 hectares, and supply all the drinking water of Nouakchott and Saint-Louis and 60 per cent of Dakar's.

sources.title: Convention establishing the Senegal River Development Organization
L'Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Senegal montre l'exemple d'une gestion concertee de l'eau

Société Nationale pour le Développement.desc: Mauritanian state body for irrigated farming, set up in 1975 as a public institution of a commercial and industrial character with its own legal personality and budget. It promotes irrigated agriculture, builds and maintains irrigation works such as canals, dykes and water channels, and gives technical advice and input support to small farmers and collective irrigated farms.

sources.title: Presentation
sources.publisher: Societe Nationale pour le Developpement Rural (SONADER)

Nepal Intermodal Transport Development B.desc: Nepali government board that develops and oversees the country's inland clearance depots (dry ports) and intermodal freight transport, formed under a 1998 formation order and chaired by the secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. It leases depot operation to private firms chosen by tender, sets terminal charges, and signs rail cargo agreements with Indian Railways; its depots include Birgunj, Biratnagar, Bhairahawa, Kakarbhitta and Tatopani.

sources.title: Nepal: country presentation on dry ports and intermodal transport

Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Suppl.desc: Nepali government ministry, based at Singha Durbar in Kathmandu, that handles industrial policy and investment, domestic and foreign trade, supply management and consumer protection. The Department of Industry, the Department of Commerce, Supply and Consumer Protection and the Office of the Company Registrar sit under it, along with state firms including Nepal Oil Corporation.

sources.title: Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies (official site)

Nepal Electricity Authority.desc: Nepal's state electricity utility, which generates, transmits and distributes power across the country and advises the government on power policy and tariffs. It began work on 16 August 1985 under the Nepal Electricity Authority Act 1984, formed by merging the Department of Electricity, the Nepal Electricity Corporation and several power development boards.

sources.title: About Us

Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and.desc: Nepali government ministry responsible for roads, railways and transport services. Four bodies sit under it: the Department of Roads, the Department of Transport Management, the Railway Department and the Nepal Shipping Office, and its divisions include one for highways and alternative transport.

sources.title: Departments under the ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Government of Nepal

National Highway Authority.desc: Pakistani government authority in charge of the national road network. Pakistan's Economic Survey for 2024-25 says it manages 48 national highways, motorways and strategic roads totalling 14,480 km.

sources.title: Pakistan Economic Survey, chapter on Transport and Communication
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan

Land Revenue Departments of Khyber Pakht.note: The key groups two separate provincial/territorial bodies under a collective label rather than naming either as it is officially titled. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Board of Revenue site (kpbor.gov.pk) and the Pakistan National Highway Authority site (nha.gov.pk) both refused WebFetch (robots or client error), and no government page was opened that describes either land revenue department, let alone both. Left blank rather than describe a generic provincial revenue department.

Electrocentro.desc: Peruvian electricity distribution company, legally Empresa Regional de Servicio Publico de Electricidad del Centro S.A., which buys power from generators and sells it in a concession area covering parts of Junin, Pasco, Ayacucho, Huanuco and Huancavelica and smaller areas in five other departments; it also runs transmission lines and some small hydro plants. The state holding company FONAFE owns all its shares, and it had 920,092 customers in November 2022.

sources.title: Informe de Transferencia de Gestion, Electrocentro S.A. (26.11.2022 al 10.12.2022)

Hidrandina.desc: Peruvian electricity distribution company serving La Libertad, Ancash and seven provinces of Cajamarca, with a concession area of about 8,570 square kilometres; it also runs public lighting and rural electrification work. It belongs to the Grupo Distriluz and the state holding company FONAFE holds more than 95 per cent of its capital. In 2024 it had 1,091,095 customers and 758 direct employees.

sources.title: Reporte de Sostenibilidad 2024

Dirección General de Electrificación Rur.desc: Unit of Peru's Ministry of Energy and Mines that plans and carries out rural electrification projects, created by Supreme Decree 026-2007-EM and working under the General Rural Electrification Law (Law 28749) and its 2020 regulation. It coordinates with regional and local governments and with the distribution utilities, assessing demand, networks and project costs before works go ahead.

sources.title: Presentation to the Congress Energy and Mines Committee on rural electrification
sources.publisher: Ministerio de Energia y Minas / Congreso de la Republica del Peru

Manila Water Company, Inc..desc: Philippine water utility that treats and distributes water and provides sewerage and sanitation services in the East Zone of Metro Manila and Rizal province, covering 24 cities and towns over about 1,400 square kilometres and serving more than seven million people. It was incorporated in 1997, began operating in 2000, listed its shares in March 2005, and its own profile gives Trident Water as controlling shareholder with 52.16 per cent, alongside Philwater Holdings (19.01 per cent) and Ayala Corporation (12.26 per cent); its concession with MWSS runs to 2037.

sources.title: Business Profile

Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage Sys.desc: Philippine government corporation created by Republic Act 6234, approved on 19 June 1971, which abolished the National Waterworks and Sewerage Authority and took over its assets and staff. It builds, maintains and operates water and sewerage systems in and around Manila, sets water and sewerage charges, and regulates and supervises other waterworks and deepwells in its area.

sources.title: An Act Creating the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (RA 6234)

Land Bank of the Philippines.desc: Philippine state bank, wholly owned by the national government, operating under its charter Republic Act 3844 of 1963 as amended (most recently by Republic Act 10878 in 2016). It runs ordinary commercial banking and uses the profits to fund rural development lending, with small farmers and fishers, many of them agrarian reform beneficiaries, as a priority group; its own site describes it as the largest formal credit institution in rural areas and among the country's five biggest commercial banks by deposits, assets and loans.

sources.title: Annual Corporate Governance Report 2024
About Us

Maynilad Water Services, Inc..desc: Philippine water utility supplying piped water and sewerage and septic-tank services to 17 cities and towns in the West Zone of Metro Manila and parts of Cavite, as the private concessionaire of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System. The 25-year concession was granted in 1997 and a revised agreement signed in May 2021 runs it to 31 July 2037; the company is held through Maynilad Water Holdings, a joint venture of Metro Pacific Investments, DMCI Holdings and Marubeni Corporation, which took control in January 2007.

sources.title: Our Company

Dragonhart.note: The key gives only the single word 'Dragonhart', with no legal suffix. Searches surfaced a Philippine firm, Dragonhart Construction Enterprise Inc., on job boards and a commercial database, but no page was opened that ties that firm to this project or that gives a company description from a primary source. Treating the two as the same entity would be a guess, so left blank.

National Irrigation Administration.desc: Philippine government-owned corporation responsible for developing and running the country's irrigation systems, created by Republic Act 3601 on 22 June 1963 and given wider powers by Presidential Decrees 552 (1974) and 1702 (1980). Its 2024 annual report says it operated and maintained 262 national irrigation systems with a combined service area of 980,108 hectares as of December 2024.

sources.title: Annual Report 2024

Laguna Lake Development Authority.desc: Philippine government body created by Republic Act 4850, approved on 18 July 1966, to plan and manage development around Laguna de Bay, covering the provinces of Rizal and Laguna and several cities including Manila and Quezon City. It prepares the region's development plan, clears projects there, is the only body that may issue permits for uses of the lake such as fishpens and navigation, sets water quality standards and may undertake its own works.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 4850 (full text)
sources.publisher: Asian Development Bank, Law and Policy Reform

Municipal Government of Rodriguez, Rizal.desc: Local government of Rodriguez, also known as Montalban, a municipality in Rizal province next to Metro Manila. The 2020 census counted 443,954 residents, making it the second most populous local government in Rizal after the city of Antipolo.

sources.title: 2020 Census of Population and Housing, Region IV-A press release

Regional Authority for Water Management.desc: Polish state water management body seated in Gliwice, covering towns in the Silesian region. Since 1 January 2018 it has been one of eleven regional water management boards of Panstwowe Gospodarstwo Wodne Wody Polskie, the state water body created by the 2017 Water Law; the boards carry out water-law duties in their area, give opinions on planning, infrastructure and environmental decisions, and act as the economic regulator for water supply and sewerage.

sources.title: Rozporzadzenie nadajace statut Panstwowemu Gospodarstwu Wodnemu Wody Polskie (Dz.U. 2017 poz. 2506)
Rozporzadzenie w sprawie wlasciwosci miejscowej dyrektorow regionalnych zarzadow gospodarki wodnej Wod Polskich (Dz.U. 2018 poz. 510)

Lower Silesian Board for Amelioration an.desc: Polish public body based in Wroclaw, a budget unit of the Lower Silesian voivodeship self-government, whose stated field of work was building and maintaining waters and water structures under the water law, including drainage and land reclamation records. From 1 January 2018 the 2017 Water Law moved the voivodeship marshals' water maintenance duties to the new state body Panstwowe Gospodarstwo Wodne Wody Polskie.

sources.title: Contract award notice 106898-2017, Dolnoslaski Zarzad Melioracji i Urzadzen Wodnych we Wroclawiu
Nowe Prawo wodne - informacje dla gmin po szkoleniu
sources.publisher: Zwiazek Gmin i Powiatow Subregionu Centralnego Wojewodztwa Slaskiego

Palestinian Energy and Natural Resources.desc: Palestinian Authority body that governs the energy sector. Under Article 4 of Decree-Law 13 of 2009, the General Electricity Law, it sets sector policy, issues safety rules and codes, proposes tariffs and licences energy projects for approval by the Council of Ministers, grants and approves transfers of distribution and generation licences, and works on renewable energy.

sources.title: Decree-Law No. 13 (2009) regarding the General Electricity Law
sources.publisher: UNEP Law and Environment Assistance Platform (FAOLEX record)

Israel Electric Corporation.desc: Israel's main electricity company, working across generation, transmission, distribution and supply, with transmission and distribution now its focus. The State of Israel held 99.85 per cent of its shares as of May 2025. Its investor presentation gives 9,474 MW of generating capacity across 42 units in 2024, about 3.0 million customers at 31 December 2024, 10,055 employees and revenue of ILS 26,184 million for 2024.

sources.title: Investors Presentation 2025

Electrogaz.desc: Rwanda's former state water and electricity utility. It began as REGIDESO in 1939 and took the name Electrogaz in 1976. A law of 9 September 2008 split it into the Rwanda Energy Company (RECO) and the Rwanda Water and Sanitation Company (RWASCO); those two were merged in 2010 into the Energy, Water and Sanitation Authority, which was itself unbundled in 2014 into the Rwanda Energy Group and the Water and Sanitation Corporation.

sources.title: History

Energy Water and Sanitation Authority, R.desc: Rwanda's former state utility for electricity, water and sanitation, created in 2010 by merging the Rwanda Energy Company and the Rwanda Water and Sanitation Company, which had been split off from Electrogaz in 2008. A law of 31 January 2014 repealed the law that set it up, and in July 2014 its work passed to two new wholly state-owned companies, the Rwanda Energy Group and the Water and Sanitation Corporation; a Prime Minister's Order of 16 August 2014 transferred its property and duties.

sources.title: History
History

Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resou.desc: Rwandan government ministry for farming and livestock, working to raise food supply, exports and farm productivity under the 2018 National Agricultural Policy and its fifth Strategic Plan for the Transformation of Agriculture. Its directorates general cover planning, agriculture modernisation, animal resources, and value chains and trade.

sources.title: About the Ministry
sources.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources, Republic of Rwanda

Companhia Santomense de Telecomunicações.desc: Telecommunications operator in Sao Tome and Principe, founded in 1990, which began with a fixed analogue network and later added mobile service, and now sells fixed and mobile telephone and internet service to households and businesses. In February 2022 the Portuguese group Visabeira Global agreed to buy the 51 per cent stake held by Africatel, a holding controlled by Brazil's Oi, with the state of Sao Tome and Principe keeping 49 per cent; a Visabeira release in 2025 describes the company as owned by Visabeira and the government.

sources.title: Visabeira buys 51% of telecoms operator CST
Companhia Santomense de Telecomunicacoes - 35 anos (press release)

Agência Fiduciária de Administração de P.desc: Agency in Sao Tome and Principe that handles the money side of donor-funded projects, headed by a general director. In World Bank grant agreements it signs as the project implementing entity and carries out the fiduciary work for government ministries: procurement, financial management, disbursement, monitoring and reporting, audits and a complaints line.

sources.title: Project Agreement for Additional Financing Grant D778-ST
Implementation status report, Sao Tome and Principe Institutional Capacity Building project

BOTAS Petroleum Pipeline Corporation.desc: Turkish state oil and gas company, in full Boru Hatlari ile Petrol Tasima Anonim Sirketi, which moves crude oil by pipeline, imports and transmits natural gas, and runs storage, tariff and port services. Turkey's state audit office lists it among the 25 state economic enterprises governed by Decree-Law 233 and shows its current assets at about 506 billion lira at the end of 2023.

sources.title: 2023 yili Kamu Isletmeleri Genel Raporu
About Us

State Road Agency of Ukraine (Ukravtodor.desc: Ukraine's national roads body, responsible for building, repairing and maintaining state-owned roads. In January 2023 it was folded into a new central executive body, the State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development, formed on the base of Ukravtodor and Ukrinfraproekt, which now also handles reconstruction of housing, social, energy and transport facilities and border crossing points, under the minister for recovery, infrastructure and transport.

sources.title: About the Agency
sources.publisher: State Agency for Restoration and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine

Bukhara Regional Production State Enterp.desc: Water and sewerage utility for the Bukhara region of Uzbekistan, one of 14 regional Suvokova unitary enterprises created in a sector reform; World Bank reports name it as the Bukhara implementing agency for work on the city's wastewater treatment plant and sewer network, recording 34 km of sewers replaced and 12.4 km built by late 2020. A 2019 presidential decree converted the state unitary water supply enterprises in the housing and communal services system into limited liability companies and created the joint-stock company Uzsuvtaminot from them; by 2025 the Bukhara region water and sewerage projects were being run by the joint-stock company Bukhara Suv Ta'minoti under Uzsuvtaminot.

Specific Procurement Notice, Bukhara Region Water Supply and Sewerage Project Phase 1

Projects Implementation Unit for Water I.desc: Uzbek government unit that runs donor-financed irrigation and drainage projects: it oversees the construction works, picks farmers for demonstration plots with water user associations and local authorities, handles complaints and works with supervision and monitoring consultants. The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources was split in February 2018 into a Ministry of Agriculture and a Ministry of Water Resources, and World Bank reporting from 2021 describes the unit as sitting under the Ministry of Water.

sources.title: Implementation Status and Results Report, Ferghana Valley Water Resources Management Phase II (P149610), Sequence No. 09
Uzbek agriculture and water resources ministry split into two

Ministry of Transport, Works, Urban Deve.desc: Government ministry of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines. A gazette of 10 November 2017 assigning ministerial responsibilities under the 1979 constitution gave it roads and traffic, sea and river defences, public buildings and works, the electrical inspectorate, urban development, local government and postal services.

sources.title: Extraordinary Gazette No. 59 of 2017, assignment of ministerial responsibilities
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Central Planning Division, Ministry of F.desc: Unit inside the finance ministry of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines that coordinates and runs externally financed government projects. In a World Bank project operations manual it is named the main coordinating body, handling procurement, disbursement paperwork, project accounts, monitoring and evaluation and environmental and social safeguards, drawing on line ministries for technical work. The ministry held the economic planning portfolio under the November 2017 assignment of ministerial responsibilities.

sources.title: Regional Disaster Vulnerability Reduction Project, Operations Manual (November 2014)
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

sources.title: Extraordinary Gazette No. 59 of 2017, assignment of ministerial responsibilities
sources.publisher: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Korporata Energjetike e Kosoves (KEK).desc: Kosovo's state-owned electricity generator, which runs the lignite-fired Kosovo A and Kosovo B power stations; Kosovo B also supplies heat to the Pristina district heating company. More than 90 per cent of Kosovo's electricity comes from coal, mostly from these two plants. Kosovo's energy ministry says five generating units were running at the end of 2025, three at Kosovo A and two at Kosovo B, and that a 2025 turbine upgrade added about 35 MW at one Kosovo B unit.

sources.title: Energy prices and subsidies in Kosovo, in Energy Prices and Subsidies in the Western Balkans
Prime Minister Kurti and Minister Rizvanolli visit the Kosovo Energy Corporation
sources.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Republic of Kosovo

Ministry of Environment and Spatial Plan.desc: Kosovo government ministry for the environment and spatial planning, re-established after 2000. In the 2021 state of the environment report it appears under the wider name Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure; it puts the annual state of the environment report to the government and its inspectorate carries out environmental inspections, such as checks on river sand and gravel operators between 2019 and 2021.

sources.title: Report on the State of the Environment 2021

rePlan Inc..desc: Canadian consulting firm based in Toronto and founded in 1978, which advised natural resource and infrastructure companies and financial institutions on social impact and risk. The environmental consultancy ERM announced on 11 August 2015 that it had bought the business, which the trade press reports under the name rePlan.

sources.title: ERM acquires Canadian social impact and risk specialist

Road Development Agency, Zambia.desc: Zambian government agency responsible for the care, maintenance and construction of public roads, set up under the Public Roads Act No. 12 of 2002 (amended by Act No. 9 of 2022) and operating since 2006; it also sets maximum vehicle weights and runs the national road tolling programme under the Tolls Act of 2011. Its 2022 annual report puts the classified network in its charge at 67,671 km, of which it concentrates on a core network of 40,454 km.

sources.title: Annual Report 2022
